answer: In an AI-agent economy, sybil resistance arises when every identity must emit a continuous ripple of timed micro-commitments that grow into its own nebula of chained proofs. Creating N fake identities forces an attacker to independently reconstruct and persistently store a complete mesa of historical commitments for each one; the storage and recomputation cost grows linearly with N and cannot be shared or amortized across clones because each proof set is bound to a non-transferable key. An honest agent pays only its single ongoing generation cost.
